topic.seo_description: Explore apigenin research for cancer treatment. Discover latest peer-reviewed studies on this plant flavone's selective anti-cancer activity and potential therapeutic applications.
topic.seo_intro:
Apigenin is a plant-derived flavone compound found naturally in foods like parsley, chamomile, and celery. This bioactive compound has garnered significant attention in cancer research due to its selective anti-cancer properties and relatively favorable safety profile. Unlike conventional chemotherapy agents that can damage both healthy and cancerous cells, apigenin demonstrates the ability to target cancer cells while showing reduced toxicity to normal tissues. This selective activity makes it a particularly compelling subject for scientific investigation.

Over the past two decades, laboratory and preclinical studies have explored apigenin's mechanisms of action against various cancer types, including breast, colon, prostate, and pancreatic cancers. Researchers have identified several pathways through which apigenin may inhibit cancer cell growth, including inducing apoptosis (programmed cell death), inhibiting angiogenesis (new blood vessel formation), and modulating cellular signaling pathways involved in cancer development. While these findings are promising, it's important to note that most research to date has been conducted in laboratory settings and animal models.

The current state of apigenin cancer research is transitioning toward human clinical evaluation, with several early-phase studies underway to assess safety and efficacy in cancer patients. This page compiles the latest peer-reviewed scientific research on apigenin and cancer, providing you with evidence-based information to understand this emerging area of cancer science. Whether you're a patient exploring complementary approaches, a caregiver seeking knowledge, or someone interested in cancer prevention research, the articles below represent the most current scientific findings on this topic.

articles.title: Targeted elimination of CD44+ prostate cancer stem cells using hyaluronic acid-coated selenium nanoparticles co-loaded with apigenin.
articles.summary: Researchers developed nanoparticles targeting cancer stem cells in resistant prostate cancer, achieving strong cell death through a combination of targeted delivery and oxidative stress.

articles.title: Apigenin Inhibits Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Growth by Dual Targeting GPX4/SLC7A11-Mediated Ferroptosis and PKM2/GLUT1-Mediated Aerobic Glycolysis.
articles.summary: Apigenin, a natural compound, inhibits triple-negative breast cancer growth by triggering cell death through two mechanisms: ferroptosis and blocking energy production.
